payload.title: lift_sandbox_pin reads each lifted file with an unbounded handle.read() and the pin admission bounds the number of files but not their size, so a multi-gigabyte test file the seat writes is loaded into kernel memory
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/validation.py:553-562 (_admit_pin checks the files dict for count and type, not for size)
payload.rule_violated: Untrusted input is bounded where it is read (root CLAUDE.md, Security: input validation): what a seat can make the kernel hold has a limit
payload.notes: Registered by the D6 findings clerk from the D6 review round 1 (lens security), re-checked at head ac106b734 before registration; non-blocking at merge. Close condition: A named byte limit per file and for the pin as a whole, applied by _admit_pin (so the prover refuses an oversized pin too) and enforced in the lift by reading at most the limit plus one byte. Test: a lifted file one byte over the limit is refused by name without the rest being read.
